title: Why You Must Stop Coddling Your Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin makes a forceful argument that the well-meaning softening of behavior standards during the pandemic — expanded boundaries, tolerated disrespect, lowered academic expectations — has actively harmed students rather than protected them. He characterizes the instinct to explain away misbehavior as trauma ('they've been through so much') as a dangerous overcorrection that must end immediately. His alternative is for teachers to shoulder more responsibility, not less: raising standards, setting firm boundaries, and demanding accountability, which he claims restores the sense of purpose and stability students are actually craving. He frames excessive pandemic-era safety measures as having gone past the point of protecting students into actively undermining their motivation and mental health, and urges teachers to accept personal risk as part of the job, just as other essential workers did. He ends by describing renewed purpose and accountability as a mutual gift — improving both student behavior and teacher wellbeing.
points: Expanding tolerance for disrespect and lowering academic standards during the pandemic has harmed students rather than protected them.
Firm boundaries and high expectations, not accommodation, are what students actually crave and respond to as a sign that someone cares.
Teachers must resist the pressure to excuse misbehavior as unavoidable trauma and instead raise standards immediately.
Excessive caution and restriction, past a certain point, destroy the purpose, inspiration, and motivation students need.
Taking on the responsibility of raising standards for students also restores a sense of purpose and reduces stress for the teacher.
quotes: Out of fear of hurting them even more, we in education have taken the foot completely off the gas. Behavior boundaries have been expanded or removed entirely.
Nonsense. It must end now. We’ve traveled so far down the placation highway that we may not be able to get back.
They must ask for, expect, and demand exemplary behavior from all students. They must set their boundaries in cement and teach like they’re blazing right back up that highway on a Ducati 1199.
Safety is important until it does more harm than it helps. Too much, too long, or too restrictive, beyond the common risks of living life, destroy purpose, inspiration, and motivation.
You’re given a life mission. You’re given drive and a chance to make a more profound mark on the world than if we’d never heard of Covid-19.
Their behavior improves. They sit up straighter in their seats. Happiness and laughter return to your classroom.
